newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt experts dig up cancer in ancient skull.
newsitem.headline: Egypt experts dig up cancer in ancient skull.

text.p: Egyptian experts said on Monday that they have found early evidence of cancer in the skull of a workman who helped build the Giza pyramids 4,600 years ago.

"In our excavations of the tombs of the workmen who built the pyramids we found two cemeteries. In the lower cemetery of the workmen who moved the stones to build the pyramid we found one skull. It's very important," said archaeologist Zahi Hawas, director of the Giza plateau where the pyramids are.

"We did analysis of that skull through the National Research Centre. It is the first time in archaeology that you see one individual dated back to 4,600 years ago and he had cancer," he told Reuters television.
Hawas said that the skull and other finds of bones at the tombs could help increase the understanding of medical practices in ancient Egypt.
The skull was peppered at its top with holes ranging from the size of a large coin to a pea.
Azza Ezzeddin, researcher at the centre, said the man was about 35 to 40 years old when he died.
She said the lesions in the skull and others they found in his ribs point to a diagnosis of carcinoma, a type of cancer.
